The analyses behind the main-text decision-curve figures, in one place. Code is hidden; each
chunk regenerates its figure under `figures/`.

```{r setup}
#| include: false
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
                      fig.align = "center", dpi = 150)
suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(dcurves); library(dplyr); library(ggplot2); library(data.table)})
HERE <- ".."                                      # this .qmd lives in manuscript/; repo root is ..
for (f in list.files(file.path(HERE, "R"), "^fn_.*\\.R$", full.names = TRUE)) source(f)
```

## Baseline decision curve

One SDM at a fixed landscape prevalence, the standard way (the `dcurves` package, so the
canonical treat-all / treat-none references come along), with the summary-metric route (a
binormal ROC fit to the model's reported PR-AUC) overlaid on the exact per-point curve.

```{r baseline}
#| include: false
## The hold-out sample is enriched (~0.52 presence), so we pass the landscape prevalence via
## dca()'s `prevalence=` (its case-control adjustment) rather than reweighting by hand.
PI   <- 0.025
EX   <- "1arc-Iteration1-PA1:30DO:0-Seed5101"   # spatial-mapping, 1:30 P:A (hold-out prev ~3.3%)

h <- read.csv(file.path(HERE, "data", "holdout_point_predictions.csv")) |>
  filter(model == EX, calibration == "raw", design == "spatial_mapping")

PT_MARK <- 0.20 # "happy to survey 5 sites to find 1" -> p_t = 1/5
PT_GRID <- seq(0.001, 0.50, by = 0.005)
d <- dca(Presence ~ prob, data = h, prevalence = PI,
         thresholds = PT_GRID, # run high so the SDM decay is visible (illustrative)
         label = list(prob = "SDM"))

## SUMMARY-METRIC route: fit an equal-variance binormal ROC (mu) reproducing the model's PR-AUC at
## its design prevalence, then read net benefit at the ROC point whose slope equals the cost ratio.
## ap_pointwise(), ap_binormal(), nb_binormal(): see R/fn_average_precision.R, R/fn_net_benefit.R
pi_hold  <- mean(h$Presence)
pr_hold  <- ap_pointwise(h$Presence, h$prob, pi_hold)      # the number a paper would report
mu_fit   <- uniroot(function(m) ap_binormal(m, pi_hold) - pr_hold, c(1e-3, 8))$root
nb_bin   <- nb_binormal(mu_fit, PI, PT_GRID)               # best-achievable NB from the fitted ROC

lv <- c("SDM (per-point, exact)", "SDM (summary, binormal)",
        "Survey all (treat-all)", "Survey none (treat-none)")
nb <- as_tibble(d) |>
  transmute(strategy = recode(as.character(label),
                              "Treat All" = "Survey all (treat-all)",
                              "Treat None" = "Survey none (treat-none)",
                              "SDM" = "SDM (per-point, exact)"),
            threshold, net_benefit) |>
  bind_rows(tibble(strategy = "SDM (summary, binormal)",
                   threshold = PT_GRID, net_benefit = nb_bin)) |>
  mutate(strategy = factor(strategy, levels = lv))
is_ref  <- grepl("treat", nb$strategy)
nb_mark <- nb$net_benefit[nb$strategy == "SDM (per-point, exact)"][
             which.min(abs(nb$threshold[nb$strategy == "SDM (per-point, exact)"] - PT_MARK))]

p_baseline <- ggplot(mapping = aes(threshold, net_benefit, colour = strategy)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = PT_MARK, colour = "grey55", linetype = "dotted") +
  annotate("text", x = PT_MARK, y = PI * 1.08, hjust = -0.04, size = 3, colour = "grey35",
           label = sprintf("p[t]==0.20~': survey 5 to find 1'"), parse = TRUE) +
  annotate("point", x = PT_MARK, y = nb_mark, colour = cda_cols[["naive"]], size = 2) +
  geom_line(data = nb[is_ref, ], aes(linetype = strategy), linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_line(data = nb[!is_ref, ], linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("SDM (per-point, exact)" = cda_cols[["naive"]],
                                 "SDM (summary, binormal)" = cda_cols[["summary"]],
                                 "Survey all (treat-all)" = cda_cols[["treat_all"]],
                                 "Survey none (treat-none)" = cda_cols[["treat_none"]]), name = NULL) +
  scale_linetype_reference() +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-0.02, PI * 1.12)) +    # clip the deep treat-all tail, keep its zero-crossing
  labs(x = expression("Threshold probability  " * p[t]), y = "Net benefit",
       title = sprintf("Decision curve SDM at %.1f%% landscape prevalence", 100 * PI),
       subtitle = "Per-point (raw predictions) vs the summary route (binormal from reported PR-AUC).") +
  theme_cda()

ggsave(file.path(HERE, "figures", "dca_baseline_dcurves.png"), p_baseline, width = 9, height = 5, dpi = 150)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-baseline-dca
#| fig-cap: "Decision curve for one SDM (1:30 P:A, hold-out prevalence ~3.3%) at 2.5% landscape prevalence. The per-point and summary-metric routes track closely for this model; the marked point is the net benefit at the \"survey five to find one\" threshold."
p_baseline
```

## AOA downgrade: naive vs in-domain

The same model scored two ways at 5% prevalence — *naive* on the full hold-out, and *AOA-honest*
on the in-domain points only (presences vs the hard, environmentally-similar absences) — with both
reweighted to the same prevalence. The gap is the inflation from trivially rejecting easy, far-from-
suitable absences. (The ROC-AUC drop across all models is quantified in Appendix 2.)

{{< include _aoa_downgrade.qmd >}}

```{r}
#| label: fig-aoa-inflation
#| fig-cap: "Naive (full hold-out) vs AOA-honest (in-domain) decision curve for the example model, both at 5% prevalence. The two agree only at the broadest thresholds; the gap is the inflation contributed by easy absences, and the in-domain curve drops below \"survey none\" well before the \"survey five to find one\" tolerance."
p_aoa
```

## Patch delineation (watershed)

Delineate suitable-habitat patches on the example model's probability surface, so the main
text's "pixels to patches" unit of analysis has concrete numbers behind it. Binarize at the
sensitivity–specificity threshold and run a marker-controlled watershed on the masked surface;
cores separated by a probability drop of at least the prominence `delta` split into distinct
patches. The watershed pipeline is costly (~3e8 cells) and relies on WhiteboxTools, so the
delineated raster is cached to `data/raster/` with an input signature, and a compact summary is
written to `data/patch_delineation_summary.csv` for the manuscript to read.

```{r patch-delineation}
#| include: false
# sens_spec and delta are placeholders - real sensitivity-specificity and a tuned prominence
# are joined in later. Requires WhiteboxTools (whitebox::install_whitebox()).
suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(terra); library(whitebox)})
whitebox::wbt_verbose(FALSE)
sens_spec <- 0.35   # suitable-habitat threshold (probability units)
delta <- 0.05   # prominence: min neck depth to split two cores
min_area <- 100   # drop patches at or below this area (m^2): slivers too small to survey

rdir        <- file.path(HERE, "data", "raster")
src_tif     <- file.path(rdir, "1-3arc-Iteration1-PA1:35DO:0-Seed5001-Pr.tif")
patches_tif <- file.path(rdir, "example-patches.tif")
sig_file    <- file.path(rdir, "example-patches.sig")

pr <- terra::rast(src_tif)

# Skip the (costly, ~3e8-cell) watershed pipeline unless something that affects
# the result changed: the thresholds, or the source raster. A signature sidecar
# records those inputs; a match means the cached patches are still valid.
sig   <- paste(sens_spec, delta, min_area, basename(src_tif),
               file.info(src_tif)$size, file.mtime(src_tif), sep = "|")
fresh <- file.exists(patches_tif) && file.exists(sig_file) &&
         identical(readLines(sig_file, warn = FALSE), sig)

if (fresh) {
  patch_id <- terra::rast(patches_tif)
} else {
  mask <- pr >= sens_spec

  # Marker-controlled watershed via the hydrological inversion trick: invert the
  # probability surface so high-probability cores become pits, merge necks
  # shallower than delta (fill max_depth), label the surviving pits as seeds,
  # then route every suitable cell to the core it drains into. Intermediates
  # persist to data/raster so a partial re-run can reuse the finished steps.
  dem <- terra::ifel(mask, 1 - pr, NA)                 # cores -> pits
  terra::writeRaster(dem, file.path(rdir, "patch-dem.tif"), overwrite = TRUE)
  whitebox::wbt_fill_depressions(
    file.path(rdir, "patch-dem.tif"),
    file.path(rdir, "patch-fill.tif"),
    max_depth = delta
    )
  whitebox::wbt_sink(
    file.path(rdir, "patch-fill.tif"),
    file.path(rdir, "patch-sink.tif"),
    zero_background = TRUE
    )
  whitebox::wbt_d8_pointer(
    file.path(rdir, "patch-fill.tif"),
    file.path(rdir, "patch-pntr.tif")
    )
  whitebox::wbt_watershed(
    file.path(rdir, "patch-pntr.tif"),
    file.path(rdir, "patch-sink.tif"),
    file.path(rdir, "patch-seg.tif")
    )

  seg <- terra::rast(file.path(rdir, "patch-seg.tif"))
  seg[seg <= 0] <- NA

  # Fallback: suitable cells that drain off-mask (no interior pit, e.g. small
  # patches) keep an identity via 8-connected components, so none are dropped.
  unlab <- mask & is.na(seg)
  cc <- terra::patches(
    terra::ifel(unlab, 1, NA),
    directions = 8,
    zeroAsNA = TRUE
    ) +
    terra::global(seg, "max", na.rm = TRUE)[[1]]

  patch_id <- terra::mask(terra::cover(seg, cc), mask, maskvalues = c(NA, 0))

  # Drop sub-threshold slivers: patches whose total area is at or below min_area
  # are too small to be a meaningful survey unit, so we null them out here (once)
  # and bake the filter into the cached raster, so every downstream step inherits
  # it. Area is cell count x cell area; terra area/perimeter isn't needed on a
  # projected (equal-area-enough) grid.
  cell_area <- prod(terra::res(patch_id))
  fr        <- terra::freq(patch_id)
  keep_ids  <- fr$value[fr$count * cell_area > min_area]
  patch_id  <- terra::ifel(patch_id %in% keep_ids, patch_id, NA)

  # persist the delineated (and size-filtered) patches, record the signature
  terra::writeRaster(patch_id, patches_tif, overwrite = TRUE)
  writeLines(sig, sig_file)
}
names(patch_id) <- "patch"

# aggregate predicted probability over each patch (max and mean)
patch_max  <- terra::zonal(pr, patch_id, fun = "max",  na.rm = TRUE)
patch_mean <- terra::zonal(pr, patch_id, fun = "mean", na.rm = TRUE)
patch_prob <- merge(patch_max, patch_mean, by = "patch")
names(patch_prob) <- c("patch", "prob_max", "prob_mean")

n_patches <- nrow(patch_prob)

# GROUND TRUTH: which patches does the taxon actually occupy? Overlay the iter-2
# presences (UTM 13N, same CRS as the raster) onto the delineated patches. A
# presence that lands below sens_spec sits off every patch (patch = NA); it marks
# suitable habitat the binarization missed, not a labelling error, so we count it
# rather than drop it silently.
occ_pts    <- terra::vect(file.path(HERE, "data", "3m-presence-iter2.gpkg"))
occ_hit    <- terra::extract(patch_id, occ_pts)$patch
occ_ids    <- sort(unique(occ_hit[!is.na(occ_hit)]))  # occupied patch ids
n_points     <- length(occ_hit)
n_points_off <- sum(is.na(occ_hit))                   # presences off every patch
n_occupied   <- length(occ_ids)

# flag each patch as occupied / unoccupied for the patch-level DCA
patch_prob$occupied <- patch_prob$patch %in% occ_ids
write.csv(patch_prob,
          file.path(HERE, "data", "patch_predictions.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# compact summary for the manuscript's inline values
write.csv(
  data.frame(sens_spec = sens_spec, delta = delta, min_area = min_area,
             n_patches = n_patches, n_occupied = n_occupied,
             n_points = n_points, n_points_off = n_points_off),
  file.path(HERE, "data", "patch_delineation_summary.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE)
```

## Conceptual decision curve (illustrative — backup)

Backup of the tuned, self-contained example behind the main-text conceptual DCA figure. Not the
case-study data. The model is deliberately *miscalibrated*: a share of true presences are poorly
detected and score like absences, so (unlike a calibrated model) the curve does not dominate the
references — it dips just below *treat all* at very low $p_t$, and its tail droops as $p_t$ rises
and the model sheds sites. Kept here so the simulation parameters aren't lost; the annotated
version lives in the manuscript.

```{r conceptual-dca-backup}
#| include: false
set.seed(1)
n <- 60000
y <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.12)                              # true outcomes, ~12% prevalence

# miscalibrated model: ~half of presences weakly detected and scored like absences
miss <- runif(n) < 0.50
prob <- ifelse(y == 1 & !miss, rbeta(n, 3, 3.5),     # detected presences: moderate score
        ifelse(y == 1 &  miss, rbeta(n, 0.8, 10),    # missed presences: look like absences
                               rbeta(n, 0.5, 11)))   # absences: low score
ex <- data.frame(Presence = y, prob = prob)
PI <- mean(ex$Presence)                              # prevalence (NOT mean(prob): miscalibrated)

PT_MARK <- 0.20                                      # 1:5 ratio (treat 5 to find 1)
PT_GRID <- seq(0.001, 0.60, by = 0.005)

d <- dca(Presence ~ prob, data = ex, thresholds = PT_GRID, label = list(prob = "Model")) |>
  as_tibble()
lab <- c(Model = "Model", "Treat All" = "Treat all", "Treat None" = "Treat none")
nb  <- d |> transmute(strategy = factor(lab[as.character(label)], levels = lab),
                      threshold, net_benefit)
cols <- c("Model" = "#1b7837", "Treat all" = "#d95f02", "Treat none" = "grey45")

p_concept_backup <- ggplot(nb, aes(threshold, net_benefit, colour = strategy)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = PT_MARK, colour = "grey10", linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_line(data = subset(nb, grepl("Treat", strategy)), aes(linetype = strategy), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(data = subset(nb, strategy == "Model"), linewidth = 1.1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cols, name = NULL) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("Treat all" = "solid", "Treat none" = "22"), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-0.02, PI * 1.25), xlim = c(0, 0.50)) +
  labs(x = expression("Threshold probability  " * p[t]), y = "Net benefit",
       title = "Decision curve analysis (illustrative, miscalibrated model)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

ggsave(file.path(HERE, "figures", "conceptual_dca_backup.png"),
       p_concept_backup, width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 150)
```
